projects.title: A worker-built tool to crowdsource gig-app pay data
projects.description: As part of the $131.5 million DoorDash wage theft settlement announced September 22, 2026, the city's $4.3 million compliance fund is financing Workers Justice Project and Princeton University's Workers' Algorithm Observatory (wao.cs.princeton.edu) to build software that lets delivery workers capture what the DoorDash app shows them about their trips and pay and share that data directly with the city. DoorDash is barred from penalizing a worker for using it.
projects.why_interesting: Flips the usual script on platform data: instead of the city or a researcher scraping what a gig company publishes, workers themselves become the sensor network feeding an outside algorithm audit.

projects.title: CityCamp NYC 2026
projects.description: BetaNYC's annual civic-tech unconference drew 235 people to Hunter College on September 19, 2026, for 40 self-organized sessions spanning AI accountability, childcare-access gaps, a block-by-block mapping project for NYC's block associations, tenant data, and even a count of ant species in the city's smallest parks. Recap published September 30.
projects.why_interesting: A yearly snapshot of what NYC's civic-data volunteers are actually building next, pitched and scheduled by attendees in real time rather than set by an agency agenda.

projects.title: Epoch AI's Data Centers explorer, scaled up
projects.description: The nonprofit research group Epoch AI announced September 16, 2026 that it expanded its AI Data Centers tracker from 13 to 86 facilities, raising estimated coverage of global AI compute from 15% to 44%. A new Directory tab lets users drill into individual sites -- chip types, cooling systems -- and compare satellite imagery over time as a site grows from empty field to full campus.
projects.why_interesting: One of the only public efforts mapping the physical footprint of the AI buildout site-by-site, using satellite imagery and permits rather than relying on what the companies choose to disclose.

projects.title: Mapping the heat AI data centers dump on U.S. cities
projects.description: Bloomberg published a data visualization tracing waste heat from AI data centers across U.S. cities, part of a four-newsroom spotlight in AnyChart's September 25, 2026 DataViz Weekly roundup (alongside The Washington Post's treemap of the 50 biggest 2026 midterm donors, built from FEC filings and totaling $1.7 billion given).
projects.why_interesting: Converts an abstract policy debate over AI's energy footprint into a concrete, city-by-city thermal-impact map -- the kind of localized framing that's often missing from national AI-infrastructure coverage.
